plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. With a value of $32, the optimal action is to bid exactly $32, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay a fair price when I do.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value risks overpaying, and bidding below reduces my chances of winning at a profitable price. With a value of $6, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $6, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay less than my value if I win.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid, shading my bid provides no benefit and only risks losing a profitable auction, while overbidding risks a loss. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $17 to maximize expected profit.
